records.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU) (es)
records.text: La quimioterapia de 1957 que sigue siendo la base del tratamiento de los cánceres de intestino, estómago, páncreas, ano, cabeza y cuello y mama, y que se usa en crema para las lesiones precancerosas de la piel.

records.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU) (zh)
records.text: 这种1957年问世的化疗药物至今仍是肠癌、胃癌、胰腺癌、肛门癌、头颈癌和乳腺癌治疗的基石，也以乳膏形式用于皮肤癌前病变。

records.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU) (pt)
records.text: A quimioterapia de 1957 que continua sendo a base do tratamento dos cânceres de intestino, estômago, pâncreas, ânus, cabeça e pescoço e mama, e que é usada em creme para lesões pré-cancerosas da pele.

records.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU) (hi)
records.text: 1957 की यह कीमोथेरेपी आज भी आंत, पेट, अग्न्याशय, गुदा, सिर और गर्दन तथा स्तन के कैंसर के इलाज की रीढ़ है, और त्वचा की कैंसर-पूर्व अवस्थाओं के लिए क्रीम के रूप में भी इस्तेमाल होती है।

records.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU) (fr)
records.text: La chimiothérapie de 1957 qui reste le pilier du traitement des cancers de l'intestin, de l'estomac, du pancréas, de l'anus, de la tête et du cou et du sein, et qui s'utilise en crème pour les lésions précancéreuses de la peau.

records.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU) (de)
records.text: Die Chemotherapie aus dem Jahr 1957, die bis heute das Rückgrat der Behandlung von Darm-, Magen-, Bauchspeicheldrüsen-, Anal-, Kopf-Hals- und Brustkrebs bildet und als Creme gegen Krebsvorstufen der Haut eingesetzt wird.

records.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU) (ja)
records.text: 1957年に登場した化学療法薬で、今も大腸がん、胃がん、膵臓がん、肛門がん、頭頸部がん、乳がんの治療の中心であり、皮膚の前がん病変にはクリームとしても使われている。

records.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU) (ar)
records.text: العلاج الكيميائي الذي ظهر عام 1957 ولا يزال يشكّل العمود الفقري لعلاج سرطانات الأمعاء والمعدة والبنكرياس والشرج والرأس والعنق والثدي، ويُستخدم أيضًا على شكل كريم لعلاج الآفات السابقة للسرطان في الجلد.

records.name: Chemotherapy (simple)
records.text: Chemotherapy medicines affect different cell processes. They can kill cancer cells or slow their growth, and healthy cells can be affected too.

records.name: Cytotoxic chemotherapy (simple)
records.text: These medicines can kill cancer cells or stop their growth. Their benefits and harms depend on the drug, treatment plan and cancer setting.

records.name: Alkylating agents and antimetabolites (simple)
records.text: These are two different drug families. Alkylating agents attach chemical groups to molecules such as DNA; antimetabolites interfere with chemicals cells normally use.

records.name: Capecitabine (simple)
records.text: The body converts capecitabine tablets into fluorouracil. Taking a medicine by mouth does not remove the risk of serious harm.

records.name: Fluorouracil (5-FU) (simple)
records.text: Fluorouracil is the 1957 chemotherapy that remains the backbone of treatment for bowel, stomach, pancreatic, anal and head and neck cancers, and a cream for skin precancers.

records.name: Platinum agents (simple)
records.text: Platinum medicines can attach to DNA and link sites together. That does not by itself show that a cell dies or that a treatment will work.

records.name: Taxanes (paclitaxel, docetaxel, nab-paclitaxel) (simple)
records.text: Taxanes change how microtubules grow and shorten. These structures help cells divide and do other jobs, so healthy tissue can be affected too.

records.name: Anthracyclines (doxorubicin, epirubicin) (simple)
records.text: Anthracyclines affect DNA and an enzyme that cuts and reseals it. They can also harm the heart, sometimes after treatment has ended.

records.name: Topoisomerase-I inhibitors (and ADC payloads) (simple)
records.text: These medicines can trap an enzyme on DNA during a temporary cut. Further damage depends on the medicine, exposure and cell response.

records.name: Tubulin (microtubules) (simple)
records.text: Tubulin builds microtubules used in division, transport and cell organisation. Medicines can change these structures without every exposed cell dying.

effective.effectiveText: Chemotherapy uses medicines to kill cancer cells or stop their growth. Different medicines disturb different cell processes, and their benefits and harms depend on the treatment and setting.
Cytotoxic chemotherapy can kill cancer cells or stop their growth by disturbing cell processes. Healthy cells can be affected too, and each drug and regimen needs its own evidence.
Alkylating agents and antimetabolites are different chemotherapy families. Some attach chemical groups to DNA; others interfere with the cell’s use of building blocks.
Capecitabine is an oral prodrug that the body converts to fluorouracil. It is used in specified cancer treatments, and oral delivery does not remove the risk of serious toxicity.

La quimioterapia de 1957 que sigue siendo la base del tratamiento de los cánceres de intestino, estómago, páncreas, ano, cabeza y cuello y mama, y que se usa en crema para las lesiones precancerosas de la piel.
Platinum medicines can attach to DNA and link sites together. The resulting injury, healthy-tissue effects and treatment benefit depend on the drug, exposure and cancer setting.

Taxanes disturb the normal growth and shortening of microtubules, structures used in cell division and other cell jobs. Their formulation, exposure and effects on healthy tissue matter as well as tumour activity.

Anthracyclines are chemotherapy medicines that disturb DNA and an enzyme that cuts and reseals it. They can also harm the heart, including after treatment, so prior exposure and heart function matter.
These medicines can trap an enzyme on DNA while it is making a temporary cut. This can cause further damage during copying, but the exact drug, exposure and cell response determine what follows.

Tubulin proteins build microtubules, structures used in cell division, organisation and transport. Different medicines disturb their dynamics in different ways; a disturbed microtubule does not by itself prove cell death.
